definition: An immutable packaged filesystem and configuration used to create containers.
watch_for: An image tag is a movable name; a digest identifies particular content.

definition: A running or stopped instance created from an image, with its own writable layer and configured isolation.
watch_for: Removing the container removes its writable layer; a separately managed volume has a different lifecycle.

definition: The first process in a PID namespace, with special responsibilities for signal handling and reaping child processes.
watch_for: A shell wrapper that does not forward signals can prevent graceful application shutdown.

definition: A filesystem change stored as part of an image and combined with other layers when a container starts.
watch_for: Deleting a secret in a later layer does not remove the bytes from an earlier layer.

definition: The files made available to an image build for operations such as COPY.
watch_for: A correct Dockerfile cannot copy a file excluded from its context, and an oversized context can include unintended material.

definition: Previously produced build results that can be reused when the builder considers their inputs unchanged.
watch_for: A cached step does not mean a remote dependency was checked again; choose reproducible inputs and inspect the resulting artifact.

definition: A Dockerfile with multiple build stages, allowing selected artifacts to be copied into a separate final image.
watch_for: The final image must still include the runtime dependencies needed by the copied application.

definition: A cryptographic content identifier, commonly written as sha256 followed by a hash.
watch_for: An OCI index digest can identify a set of platform images; the ARM64 manifest has its own digest.

definition: A service that stores and distributes container image manifests and blobs.
watch_for: Successfully pushing an image does not establish that a workload has the credentials and network path needed to pull it.

definition: A selected host path made visible at a path inside a container.
watch_for: Host ownership and contents remain relevant; a mount can hide files that were already present at the container target path.

definition: Storage managed separately from a container writable layer and mounted into one or more containers.
watch_for: Persistence across container replacement is different from having a tested backup or replicated storage.

definition: A local virtual network connecting container network interfaces through a software bridge.
watch_for: A working IP path does not prove that a name resolves or that a process listens on the expected interface.

definition: A host-side address and port connected to an application port in another network namespace.
watch_for: The host port and application listening port may differ; loopback binding limits which host interfaces accept connections.

definition: A named application component whose container configuration is declared in a Compose project.
watch_for: Creation order alone does not establish dependency readiness; the application also needs retry and failure behavior.

definition: A repeated observation used to report whether a specified condition currently holds.
watch_for: The command defines what is actually tested; a process check does not necessarily exercise its dependencies.

definition: The Kubernetes components that expose the API, store cluster state, schedule Pods, and reconcile cluster-level behavior.
watch_for: Existing containers can keep running during a control-plane outage even though new changes cannot be reconciled.

definition: A controller repeatedly compares desired state with observed state and acts to reduce the difference.
watch_for: Submitting a desired state is not a synchronous guarantee that the system has reached it.

definition: Kubernetes' smallest deployable workload unit, containing one or more containers that share networking and declared volumes.
watch_for: A replacement Pod has a new identity; controllers and Services help applications tolerate that replacement.

definition: A controller for rolling out and maintaining replicated Pods through ReplicaSets.
watch_for: Its own metadata labels are different from the labels assigned to Pods in spec.template.

definition: A controller that maintains a desired count of matching Pods.
watch_for: When a Deployment owns it, changing the ReplicaSet directly can conflict with the Deployment's reconciliation.

definition: A workload controller providing stable ordinal identities and ordered behavior for Pods, with persistent claims when configured.
watch_for: Stable identity does not itself replicate the application's data or make its database highly available.

definition: A controller that places a Pod on each eligible node, commonly for networking, logs, or node-level agents.
watch_for: Eligibility depends on scheduling constraints and tolerations, not simply the total node count.

definition: A controller that runs Pods toward successful completion of a finite task.
watch_for: Retries can run application work more than once; design side effects with that possibility in mind.

definition: A controller that creates Jobs according to a schedule and its concurrency and history policies.
watch_for: Scheduling is not a guarantee of exactly-once business execution.

definition: A scope for names and many policies within one cluster.
watch_for: A namespace is not automatically a complete network or security isolation boundary.

definition: A query over labels used to select objects, such as the Pods behind a Service.
watch_for: A syntactically valid selector can match no objects or the wrong objects.

definition: A stable Kubernetes access abstraction that maps a declared port to selected backend endpoints.
watch_for: DNS can resolve the Service even while no ready backend is available.

definition: An API object describing a group of network endpoints and their readiness-related conditions for a Service.
watch_for: Inspect endpoint addresses and conditions when a Service exists but traffic fails.

definition: A Service port exposed through eligible node addresses and forwarded to Service backends.
watch_for: A NodePort is not automatically a listener on the Mac hosting a VM; the host-to-guest path must also exist.

definition: An HTTP routing API whose rules require a compatible running ingress controller to handle traffic.
watch_for: Creating an Ingress object without the corresponding controller does not create a working route.

definition: Kubernetes APIs that separate infrastructure ownership from traffic routing using resources such as GatewayClass, Gateway, and HTTPRoute.
watch_for: Accepted configuration and a programmed controller are useful evidence, but the actual request still needs verification.

definition: A Kubernetes object holding non-secret configuration values that workloads can consume as files, environment variables, or API data.
watch_for: A running process does not necessarily reread a changed mounted file, and environment variables are fixed when the container starts.

definition: A Kubernetes object intended to hold sensitive values with separate access controls and consumption mechanisms.
watch_for: Base64 encoding is not encryption; API permissions, storage protection, and application exposure still matter.

definition: A Kubernetes workload identity used when a Pod authenticates to the API.
watch_for: Authentication establishes identity; RBAC separately determines what that identity may do.

definition: Role-based access control, which grants API permissions through rules and bindings to identities.
watch_for: A namespace RoleBinding does not turn its permissions into cluster-wide access.

definition: A Kubernetes API for selecting Pods and declaring allowed network traffic, enforced by a compatible networking implementation.
watch_for: The presence of the object is not proof of enforcement; test both allowed and denied connections from the relevant source.

definition: Pod or container settings controlling aspects such as identity, Linux capabilities, privilege escalation, and filesystem behavior.
watch_for: A read-only root filesystem still needs writable mounts for legitimate scratch data.

definition: A Linux mechanism that filters a process' system calls according to a policy.
watch_for: A runtime-default profile reduces available operations but is not a replacement for least-privilege identity and application design.

definition: The declared resource amount Kubernetes uses in scheduling and related resource-accounting decisions.
watch_for: A CPU request is not a hard ceiling on CPU use.

definition: A configured resource boundary enforced by the runtime and kernel according to the resource type.
watch_for: CPU limits commonly cause throttling, while exceeding a memory limit can lead to termination.

definition: A check determining whether a container should currently receive ordinary Service traffic.
watch_for: A readiness failure does not by itself mean Kubernetes restarts the container.

definition: A check that can cause the kubelet to restart a container when its configured failure threshold is reached.
watch_for: Using a transient dependency failure as liveness can turn a recoverable outage into repeated restarts.

definition: A check that gates liveness and readiness probing until the application has completed its allowed startup period.
watch_for: A startup allowance must fit the application's real initialization behavior.

definition: A workload's request for storage with declared requirements such as capacity, access mode, and storage class.
watch_for: A Pending claim can reflect scheduling or provisioning constraints rather than a missing application file.

definition: A cluster storage resource that can be bound to a claim and has its own lifecycle and reclaim policy.
watch_for: Retain preserves the backing asset after claim release; it does not make an independent backup.

definition: A named set of provisioning parameters and policies used for storage claims.
watch_for: WaitForFirstConsumer defers binding or provisioning so scheduling constraints can be considered.

definition: The Container Storage Interface through which a storage driver integrates volume provisioning, attachment, mounting, and other supported operations.
watch_for: A static local PV does not demonstrate a CSI driver's controller and node behavior.

definition: The Container Network Interface used by networking plugins to configure container network connectivity.
watch_for: Node Ready alone does not prove cross-node traffic, DNS, or NetworkPolicy enforcement.

definition: The Container Runtime Interface used by kubelet to manage Pod sandboxes and containers through a runtime such as containerd.
watch_for: ctr is a containerd administrative client; crictl specifically observes the CRI boundary.

definition: The node agent that reconciles assigned Pods with the local runtime and reports node and workload observations.
watch_for: Containers can survive while kubelet is stopped, so verify fresh leases and service state as well as application traffic.

definition: A tool that bootstraps and maintains Kubernetes control-plane configuration and node membership.
watch_for: It does not automatically provide every surrounding system, such as a CNI installation or a redundant load balancer.

definition: A Pod supervised directly by a node's kubelet from local configuration, commonly used for kubeadm control-plane components.
watch_for: Deleting its mirror object through the API does not remove the local source manifest.

definition: The distributed key-value datastore used by Kubernetes to persist cluster API state.
watch_for: An etcd snapshot does not contain the data stored in application PersistentVolumes.

definition: The voting majority required for a consensus group to commit changes.
watch_for: A three-voter etcd cluster needs two voters; adding a fourth voter does not increase its one-member failure tolerance.

definition: Client configuration describing Kubernetes clusters, users, contexts, and the selected context.
watch_for: Embedded client keys and tokens are credentials; the file must be private and scoped to the intended environment.

definition: A protocol providing encrypted transport and authenticated peer identity when trust and identity validation are configured correctly.
watch_for: Disabling certificate verification hides an identity or trust failure instead of repairing it.

definition: A Kubernetes coordination object used for purposes such as node heartbeats and leader election.
watch_for: A recent renewal is stronger evidence of current node communication than an old Ready condition alone.

definition: A controller that adjusts workload replica counts using configured metric targets and available metrics.
watch_for: A utilization target needs meaningful resource requests and a functioning metrics path.

definition: A package manager that renders charts and manages named releases of Kubernetes resources.
watch_for: Rendered YAML, release state, and running workload behavior are separate things to inspect.

definition: A tool for composing and modifying Kubernetes manifests using bases and overlays.
watch_for: Inspect the rendered objects; a patch that applies successfully may still target an unintended field.

definition: A controller that encodes domain-specific reconciliation, commonly using custom resources.
watch_for: A custom resource definition adds an API type; a working controller must still implement its behavior.

definition: An operating model in which a controller reconciles deployed state toward declarative state recorded in a source such as Git.
watch_for: An imperative fix may be overwritten until the authoritative desired state is corrected.

definition: A service-level objective describing a target for a defined reliability indicator over a stated window.
watch_for: A target without a clear numerator, denominator, and observation window is not an actionable measurement.

definition: A software bill of materials recording identified components in an artifact.
watch_for: An inventory is not a guarantee that every vulnerability or runtime risk has been identified.

definition: Replacing a credential and updating its legitimate consumers while verifying that the retired credential no longer grants access.
watch_for: A changed Secret object alone does not prove that a running application adopted the new value.

definition: A recovery exercise that reads a backup into an appropriate environment and verifies the recovered data and application behavior.
watch_for: A backup command exiting successfully does not establish that the backup is usable.
